incidents.industry: Government, telecom, healthcare, finance, critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: A large-scale credential-harvesting operation built and continuously verified a database of working logins for internet-facing Fortinet devices; researchers found no evidence a Fortinet flaw was exploited.
incidents.impact: SOCRadar uncovered an exposed attacker server holding verified, working credentials for 30,791 devices (21,108 IPs, 8,316 domains) across 194 countries, giving the operators ready access to government and enterprise networks.

incidents.vector: Attackers began exploiting two critical FortiSandbox flaws patched in April (CVE-2026-39808 OS-command injection and CVE-2026-39813 path traversal), plus a third disclosed in June, to bypass authentication and run arbitrary commands.
incidents.impact: VulnCheck and Defused observed 49 exploitation events from 11 IPs over six days; activity so far is verification and reconnaissance, which researchers warn typically precedes a heavier wave of attacks.

incidents.victim: Open-source software supply chain (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, GitHub)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating Shai-Hulud worm variants steal developer credentials and republish trojanized packages; researchers say GitHub dismissed two formal reports of the enabling design flaws as ineligible.
incidents.impact: Deep Specter confirmed 516 live malicious packages across five ecosystems, 3,000+ affected repositories and 200+ compromised developer accounts; variants have been linked to breaches at the European Commission, Mercor, LiteLLM, GitHub and Red Hat.

incidents.victim: Chinese internet users (Silver Fox trojan victims)
incidents.vector: Chinese police dismantled the Silver Fox group, which spread its namesake trojan via phishing sites and fake app-download portals to steal funds and online assets.
incidents.impact: 67 suspects were arrested across five provinces, including the trojan's author Ji Moufei and affiliates running phishing and distribution operations — a takedown of China's largest domestic cybercrime group.

incidents.vector: A phishing campaign delivers Phantom Stealer, a fileless malware-as-a-service that runs in memory and uses heavy obfuscation to evade endpoint defenses.
incidents.impact: The malware harvests browser credentials, session cookies, financial data and crypto wallets, exfiltrating via four parallel channels (Telegram, Discord, FTP, SMTP); Fortra rates it high-severity.

incidents.vector: After Microsoft revoked 1,000+ fraudulent signing certificates and dismantled the Fox Tempest signing service, the Lorem Ipsum loader pivoted from trojanized Teams installers to ClickFix lures on compromised WordPress sites.
incidents.impact: BlueVoyant links the campaign to the Vice Society ransomware/extortion group; the ClickFix shift broadens the victim pool to anyone browsing the hijacked sites.

incidents.vector: The previously unknown group UNC6508 exploited externally facing REDCap research-data servers, deployed the custom INFINITERED backdoor, and stole administrative credentials and communications.
incidents.impact: Google found the group compromised a medical-research university in September 2023 and remained undetected until November 2025, stealing research data and credentials across academia, medicine, military and foreign-policy targets.

incidents.vector: An unattributed cyberattack disrupted Astral's services for about a week; the company disclosed no technical details and Russian government agencies are involved in the investigation.
incidents.impact: Customers lost access to tax reporting, electronic document management, cash registers and corporate email; Astral serves Russian government bodies, banks and state enterprises including Russian Post and Mosgortrans. It reports no evidence of data theft.

incidents.victim: Polish public figures and their families
incidents.vector: The GhostWriter group expanded its credential-phishing operation to personal Gmail accounts, using new phishing domains almost daily and harvesting logins plus two-factor codes.
incidents.impact: CERT Polska warns the campaign targets government officials, researchers, journalists and law-enforcement personnel — and their relatives — to steal email, contacts and documents and pivot to further targets.

incidents.vector: The cargo vessel Fitburg, carrying sanctioned Russian steel, allegedly dragged its anchor along the seabed for at least 130 km, damaging undersea cables on New Year's Eve.
incidents.impact: Finland charged the captain and bosun with damaging two telecom cables and attempting to damage eight more; the defendants deny the charges and dispute Finnish jurisdiction, echoing the earlier Eagle S cable-sabotage case.

incidents.vector: Attackers 'adopted' orphaned packages on the community AUR portal and modified install procedures to pull a malicious npm package (later a Bun script to evade detection) that installed a rootkit and infostealer.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 packages were hijacked over a weekend; affected users are urged to rotate all passwords and tokens. The number of downloads during the attack window is still being assessed.

incidents.vector: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service breaches internet-facing VPNs and firewalls, then encrypts entire networks within hours; an aggressive 90/10 affiliate split is luring experienced operators.
incidents.impact: Check Point ranks The Gentlemen the second most active ransomware group by victim count, with 332+ published victims since mid-2025 (240+ in 2026); Krebs ties the admin 'Zeta88'/'Hastalamuerte' to a Russian-language forum identity.
